facts.statement: The genus Pachyosteus was described by Jaekel in 1903.
The type species of the genus is Pachyosteus bulla, described by Jaekel in 1903.
Fossils of Pachyosteus are found in the Late Devonian Kellwasserkalk facies of Bad Wildungen, Germany, and the Famennian layers of the Holy Cross Mountains in Poland.
facts.quote: known from the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Late Devonian Bad Wildungen, Germany and from the Famennian portions of the Holy Cross Mountains of Poland

facts.statement: Pachyosteus belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the larger clade Pachyosteomorphi.
facts.quote: member of the family Selenosteidae of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which belongs to the clade Pachyosteomorphi

facts.statement: According to Rücklin (2011), Pachyosteus bulla is a basal selenosteid and the sister taxon to American genera.
facts.quote: Rücklin (2011) regards Pachyosteus bulla as a basal selenosteid, being the sister taxon of the American genera

facts.statement: Pachyosteus lived during the Frasnian stage, approximately 379 to 375.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (379 to 375.2 million years ago)
